children: Anand Rathi's research report on Jyoti CNC Automation

The company’s financials continued to be impacted in Q2FY27, led by export license-related issues at Huron, which impacted consolidated revenues and EBITDA. However, we believe these issues are temporary hiccups rather than structural changes in Huron’s business, as the company has already started receiving export licenses. The management is confident of clocking in sales of ~Rs3bn in FY27, implying Rs2-2.25bn sales in H2FY27e. Orders increased 30% y/y in Q2FY27 to Rs8.09bn, taking the OB to Rs50.82bn, providing visibility for the next 18-20 months. With the machine dispatches increasing by 44% y/y to a record 1,911, we expect the machine deliveries to improve further, as the new capacity ramps up. Raising our revenue estimate by 1-3% for FY27-29e, we maintain EBITDA margin at 26/26.5% for FY28/29e.
Accordingly, we maintain BUY rating on the stock with a TP of Rs1,275, valuing it at 40x Sep-28e TTM EPS, which implies ~31% upside from the current level.
